title: ShieldLab
excerpt: An exact tiny safety-game inspector for hand-written agent protocols. Every synchronous fixed-point obligation, winning controller move, losing rank and branching invariant/counterstrategy graph is visible. Changing only who controls a state flips the result: one-step-safe actions need not preserve safety forever.
headings: ShieldLab: a safe next step can still lose
ShieldLab: safe waiting is not arrival

title: SparseLab
excerpt: Sparse coefficients are easy to display as a feature ranking. But a sparse selected support may be a coordinate-descent tie choice rather than an identified property of the fitted prediction. SparseLab separates the supplied convex optimization problem, numerical optimality checks and coefficient ambiguity.

title: SpecLab
excerpt: Speculative decoding built from scratch in pure Python: output verified identical to target-only decoding on the tested configurations, with verification rounds counted exactly.

title: SpectralLab
excerpt: Normalized spectral clustering exposes a choice that a scatter plot can hide: which points are neighbors, and what their connection means. SpectralLab builds the affinity and normalized Laplacian explicitly, retains the eigenspace, normalizes every row and runs manual k-means. NumPy supplies the symmetric eigenvalue solve through LAPACK.
headings: A relaxation is not a discrete optimum

title: STNLab: every implied deadline needs evidence
excerpt: For tiny hand-written AI plans, inspect every implied time difference: a tight path plus a complete schedule attaining the bound, or an explicit ray proving it unbounded. Negative cycles show exactly why no schedule exists, even away from the anchor. Removing one edge returns an alternate implication path or a complete separating schedule.
headings: STNLab: every implied deadline needs evidence
STNLab - temporal bounds with attainable schedules

title: STRIPSLab: the price of ignoring delete effects
excerpt: Classical AI planning with a tiny, fully disclosed state space: zero to six Boolean facts, positive initial/goal/precondition sets, and at most eight positional unit-cost actions. Each action has add and delete sets. The real successor deletes then adds; the relaxed successor only adds. Facts absent from a state are false, not unknown.
headings: STRIPSLab: the price of ignoring delete effects
STRIPSLab search witnesses: an actual suboptimal h-add plan
STRIPSLab availability: used does not mean necessary

title: SubmodLab: a guarantee is not an optimum
excerpt: Subset selection is often described as picking the most useful or diverse data. Those descriptions can hide the objective, overlap, theorem assumptions and the gap between a greedy solution and an exact optimum. SubmodLab makes each finite decision inspectable without claiming supplied similarities have learned meaning.

title: SynthLab
excerpt: Fits the examples. Fails the function. A learner chooses the cheapest grammar expression fitting known examples; an exact finite verifier returns the first wrong input. Inspect every iteration, eliminated candidate, complete truth table and evaluation tree.

title: TagLab: the normalizer is part of the model
excerpt: TagLab trains linear-chain conditional random fields from scratch, with no tensor library, autodiff, model API or external dataset. A 39-parameter sequence score combines fixed observed features, FROM/TO label transitions and separate start/end scores. Manual log-space forward/backward produces the global partition, node and adjacent-label marginals.

v0.4: a count is not an expectation
